desc: Parse N and arrays A, B. Compute counts of -1 in A and B; if unequal, output No.
Check for fixed pairs (both A_i and B_i non-negative). If any, S is fixed to that common sum (verify consistency).
Compute fixed_A, fixed_B, max_A, max_B, and T = len(fixed_A) + len(fixed_B) - N.
If T ≤ 0 and no fixed-S conflict, output Yes (can choose S = max(max_A, max_B) and assign flexibly).
If S is fixed, verify S ≥ max_A, S ≥ max_B, and compute k(S) using frequency maps; check k(S) ≥ T.
If S is not fixed and T > 0, generate candidate S = a+b for distinct a in fixed_A and b in fixed_B, build k_map by adding min(cnt_A[a], cnt_B[b]) to each sum.
Iterate over k_map entries, find any S ≥ max(max_A, max_B) with k_map[S] ≥ T, output Yes; else No.
Test thoroughly with sample inputs and edge cases (all -1, N=2, large N, conflicting fixed sums, T>0 with multiple candidates).
Verify code handles large input efficiently (N=2000, distinct values up to 2000, candidate sums up to 4e6).
Finalize and ensure code reads from stdin and writes to stdout correctly.
